findings.title: Materials' 65-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at 15.84x forward but 33.72x trailing, a 65-point percentile gap between the two lenses. That gap is the widest in the table and implies analysts expect 113 percent earnings growth, a bet that the sector's recent profit collapse reverses sharply.

findings.title: Energy's month-long slide defies its earnings
findings.body: Energy's forward percentile dropped 22 points in a month to 41, yet its trailing P/E sits at the 80th percentile. The market is pricing in 53 percent earnings growth, but the valuation compression suggests it is not trusting that forecast.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward multiple is a bargain
findings.body: Real Estate's forward P/E of 33.45 sits at the 6th percentile of its five-year range, while its trailing multiple is at the 20th. The 33-point monthly drop in forward percentile signals a repricing that assumes a 3 percent earnings decline, a stark contrast to other sectors' growth expectations.
